title: Medicine for Rudolph
description: Count single-replacement products and find minimum steps to synthesize a molecule.
writeup:
## Approach

Part 1 is straightforward enumeration. Part 2 requires working backwards from the target molecule to `e` — the forward search space is far too large.

## Part 1

For each rule and each position where it matches in the molecule, perform the substitution and collect results in a set. The set handles deduplication automatically.

## Part 2

Work in reverse: repeatedly apply rules backwards (replacing the *output* with the *input*) to shrink the molecule toward `e`. A greedy approach — always replacing the longest match — works for AoC inputs. Shuffling rule order and retrying handles edge cases where a particular ordering gets stuck. This is much faster than BFS/DFS which would be intractable on the full-size molecule.
